modeNote: "override": ensure-vendored-tokscale.js swaps in the pinned fork build described below, and the two verify-vendored-tokscale*.js gates run against it. "upstream": ensure-vendored-tokscale.js no-ops (no download or replacement) and the plain npm-installed tokscale is authoritative — but both verify-vendored-tokscale*.js gates keep running, now against that npm-installed binary, so CI still fails if it doesn't actually cover DEFAULT_CLIENTS or regressed DSH parsing. Flip to this once package.json's tokscale dependency is bumped to an official release that already contains the commit below. The override fields (commit/baseVersion/releaseTag/platforms) stay in place either way, so flipping back to "override" for a future upstream lag is just editing this file again, not re-adding infrastructure.
commitTitle: feat(sessions): add Oh My Pi (omp) as a local session source (#1161)
baseVersionNote: The npm-installed @tokscale/cli-<platform> package.json version this override was built against. ensure-vendored-tokscale.js refuses to run if the installed package reports a different version — that means the tokscale dependency already moved and this override needs to be updated (or mode switched to "upstream") together with the lockfile bump, not silently kept.
reason: Pins reviewed upstream main through commit b4abf21f while the latest tagged npm release remains 4.13.0, adding Antigravity standalone timestamp recovery and Windows sync fallback, VS Code Copilot Chat v3 parsing, provider-specific pricing aliases, larger Cursor export syncs, and native Oh My Pi discovery. Once Token Monitor's npm lockfile moves to an official tokscale release containing commit b4abf21f or later, bump the tokscale dependency and set mode to "upstream" together — the bundled version is never faked, so tokscaleUpdater.js's existing semver comparison keeps working either way, but the lockfile bump and the mode flip both need to happen, not just an upstream release existing.
